```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

summary_tables <- tar_read(imputation_summary)
numeric_all <- tar_read(imputation_numeric_all)
levels_all <- tar_read(imputation_levels_all)
units_all <- tar_read(imputation_units_all)
settings <- tar_read(settings)

fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

Missing screen use and covariates are imputed within each unit (dataset by wave by country), `r settings$imputations` times while the engine is developed and 50 times for the confirmatory run.
A variable is imputed in a unit only where it is known for at least `r 100 * settings$impute_min_observed`% of the unit's rows.
Outcomes are read by the imputation model and never imputed for analysis.
Every dataset's imputations passed the hard checks in `review_imputation()`, or the build would have stopped.

## What was imputed

One line per variable and what became of its missing values, over all units with any.
Cells are counted once, not once per imputation.

```{r}
#| label: variables
summary_tables$variables |>
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Outcome = outcome,
    Datasets = datasets,
    Units = fmt(units),
    `Cells missing` = fmt(cells_missing),
    `Cells imputed` = fmt(cells_imputed)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: failures
failed <- units_all[
  !units_all$status %in% "imputed" &
    !grepl("^too little|^fewer rows|^not needed", units_all$status),
]
```

`r nrow(failed)` unit and variable pairs failed or were only partly imputed.

```{r}
#| label: failures-table
failed |>
  count(dataset_id, variable, status, name = "units") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Imputed against observed values

An imputed value is always one its unit observed.
Imputed values need not have the same distribution as observed ones: they differ where the children with a missing value differ from the rest.
A large gap is still worth a look.

### Screen use, in hours a day

Each line pools the units that had values imputed, over all datasets.

```{r}
#| label: numeric
pooled <- numeric_all |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id),
    mean = weighted.mean(mean, n),
    median = weighted.mean(q50, n),
    q25 = weighted.mean(q25, n),
    q75 = weighted.mean(q75, n),
    n = sum(n),
    .by = c(variable, source)
  )
pooled |>
  arrange(variable, desc(source)) |>
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Values = source,
    Datasets = datasets,
    N = fmt(n),
    Mean = round(mean, 2),
    `Lower quartile` = round(q25, 2),
    Median = round(median, 2),
    `Upper quartile` = round(q75, 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrrr")
```

The quartiles are averages of each dataset's quartiles, weighted by its number of values.

```{r}
#| label: numeric-figure
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 9
by_dataset <- numeric_all |>
  select(dataset_id, variable, source, mean) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = mean)
ggplot(by_dataset, aes(observed, imputed)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable), scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Mean of observed values (hours a day)",
    y = "Mean of imputed values",
    caption = "One point per dataset; the line is equality."
  )
```

### Covariates

The share of each category among observed and imputed values, pooled over datasets.

```{r}
#| label: levels
levels_all |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = c(variable, source, level)) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = c(variable, source)) |>
  select(variable, level, source, share) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = share) |>
  filter(coalesce(observed, 0) >= 0.02 | coalesce(imputed, 0) >= 0.02) |>
  arrange(variable, desc(observed)) |>
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Category = level,
    `Observed (%)` = round(100 * observed, 1),
    `Imputed (%)` = round(100 * imputed, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr")
```

Categories under 2% of both are not shown.

## What imputation changes for the models

The slopes of the development cells fitted on complete cases and on imputed data, by covariate tier.

```{r}
#| label: gain
summary_tables$gain |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    `Slopes, complete cases` = fmt(slopes_complete),
    `Slopes, imputed` = fmt(slopes_imputed),
    `Datasets, complete cases` = datasets_complete,
    `Datasets, imputed` = datasets_imputed,
    `Rows, complete cases` = fmt(rows_complete),
    `Rows, imputed` = fmt(rows_imputed),
    `Fitted in some imputations only` = slopes_partly_fitted
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

A slope fitted in only some imputations is not carried forward.

## How much information is missing

The fraction of information missing for a unit's slope: the share of its variance that comes from not knowing the imputed values.

```{r}
#| label: fmi
summary_tables$fmi |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    Slopes = fmt(slopes),
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Nothing imputed` = fmt(nothing_imputed),
    `Median` = round(fmi_median, 3),
    `90th percentile` = round(fmi_q90, 3),
    `Largest` = round(fmi_max, 3),
    `Over a half` = fmi_over_half,
    `Covariates differed between imputations` = design_varied
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

With `r settings$imputations` imputations these fractions are themselves rough; they settle with 50.
